Rafael / Ben — drafted note below and attached a concise redline snippet. High level: agree with Rafael's compromise path but tighten several points to mitigate open-ended royalty risk.

Redline summary (suggested language snippets):
1) Injunctive relief: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither Party's right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief shall be construed as a waiver of the limitations set forth in this Section; provided, however, that any equitable relief shall be limited to injunctive relief to prevent imminent infringement and shall not give rise to uncapped monetary obligations absent a final judgment requiring monetary awards."

2) Monetary cap & royalties: "Monetary liability arising from a third-party claim of IP infringement shall be subject to the Liability Cap equal to the greater of (a) twelve (12) months of Customer's committed Annual Recurring Spend under the applicable Order Form, or (b) three (3) times Customer's average monthly spend over the prior 12 months ('Liability Cap'). Notwithstanding the foregoing, court-ordered ongoing royalty payments shall be subject to the Liability Cap except where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct is finally adjudicated."

3) Notice/Proof & Mitigation: require prompt written notice, good-faith cooperation, Redwood's right to assume defense with counsel of its choice, and a requirement that the customer mitigate and provide supporting invoices/awards before payments are binding.

4) Escrow/Insurance: suggest commercial carveouts only where customer provides evidence of third-party award; consider requirement for Helios to carry IP infringement insurance in deals with >$1M ARR.

5) Offset/subrogation: If Redwood pays royalties and subsequently recovers from vendor/sub-licensor, Redwood shall be subrogated to the customer's rights.

Attachment: Redwood_IP_carveout_note.pdf (3-page legal memo + redline snippet).

If Helios insists on unlimited royalty exposure we should not accept without C-level approval — Ben, can you confirm escalation path and threshold? I can prepare message for the execs highlighting risk quantification.

Katie / Tom — thanks for the redline. We want to keep this moving. We can agree in principle to carve out equitable relief (injunctions) from the monetary cap. On monetary royalty exposure, Redwood cannot accept unlimited royalty obligations. Proposed commercial compromise (please see attached compromise language):

- Injunctive relief and other equitable remedies: excluded from monetary cap (Helios' request) — agreed;
- Monetary damages and court-ordered royalty payments: capped at the greater of (i) 12 months of committed spend under the Order Form, or (ii) three times the customer's average monthly spend over the prior 12 months;
- Exception: where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct has been finally adjudicated, court-ordered royalties may exceed the cap;
- Evidence: Helios must provide notice, the underlying claim and documentation (complaint, settlement demand, final judgment) and cooperate with Redwood while Redwood assumes defense;
- We are open to an insurance/escrow approach for very large deals.

Attached: MSA_compromise_terms_v1.docx (redline snippet with the compromise language). Please let us know whether Helios can accept this compromise or if your procurement team needs escalation.
